summary.title: Build Your Own Text Editor
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a minimal text editor in C, in 184 small steps, by re-creating antirez's kilo editor.
keywords: build a text editor from scratch
how to write a text editor
takeaways: Build a text editor in C by following 184 incremental steps, each adding, changing, or removing a few lines of code.
The editor is based on antirez's kilo, about 1000 lines of C in a single file with no dependencies.
Chapters cover setup, entering raw mode, raw input and output, a text viewer, a text editor, search, and syntax highlighting.
summary.summary: This is an online instruction booklet from the snaptoken tutorials that walks the reader through building a text editor in C. The editor is a modified version of antirez's kilo, roughly 1000 lines in one dependency-free file, with basic editing, syntax highlighting, and search. The booklet is organized into 184 steps, most of which can be compiled and run immediately to see the effect of the changes. The page itself is a table of contents and introduction, so the detailed content lives in the linked chapters.
